world.title: Iran attacks US bases in Middle East after reports US strike killed five at wedding party
world.description: The Iranian Red Crescent says a child was among those killed when shrapnel from a US strike hit a home. The US military says it is aware of the reports and it never targets civilians.

world.title: Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations
world.description: Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.

world.title: BBC travels inside occupied Lebanon as officials say Israel expanding positions
world.description: A BBC team joined a humanitarian mission of the UN peacekeeping force, which says Israeli troops are fortifying positions and continuing demolitions.

world.title: Why do US troops have history with this Thai city?
world.description: The BBC’s Jonathan Head looks at the links between the US troops and the resort city of Pattaya as an aircraft carrier arrives nearby after 250 days at sea.

world.title: South Korea jails care home head for sexually assaulting disabled residents
world.description: The man, surnamed Kim, was handed a 15-year prison term for abusing three residents at the facility near Seoul.

world.title: Bus crash on Egypt's Red Sea coast kills 16
world.description: Another 28 people are injured in the accident in the South Sinai governorate, officials say.

world.title: Tiger Woods to change plea after crash arrest
world.description: The golfer will be in court on Wednesday for a hearing to change his plea after being charged with driving under the influence.

world.title: Charlie Kirk murder suspect pleads not guilty as judge clears way for death penalty trial
world.description: The  23-year-old is charged with aggravated murder, a capital offence in Utah, and six other counts.

world.title: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
world.description: Major efforts to rescue hydropower workers continue as Nepal's death toll exceeds 1,000.

world.title: Jailed HK activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to foreign collusion
world.description: Wong, 29, is already in prison on subversion charges under the controversial National Security Law.

world.title: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
world.description: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at the airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes on 4 August.

world.title: Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario as Lake America after Trump order
world.description: The iPhone maker follows rival technology giant Google in relabelling the Great Lake.

world.title: Ariana Grande makes emotional tour exit and steps back from public life
world.description: The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".

world.title: Remarkable US oil deal puzzles analysts - and angers many Venezuelans
world.description: Amounting to 65 billion barrels of crude, the deal is labelled by one ex-envoy as a colonialist "fever dream".

world.title: Could the man who murdered a Christian missionary and his sons walk free in India?
world.description: Dara Singh is serving a life sentence for burning alive Graham Staines and his two sons in Odisha in 1999.

US.title: U.S. military strikes Iran, while Trump vows more for Tehran's retaliation
US.description: The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday and Tehran fired missiles and drones at various sites across the region in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war.

US.title: Incumbent Sen. Ed Markey wins Massachusetts' Democratic primary for US Senate
US.description: Bucking a push for younger leadership this election season, Sen. Ed Markey, 80, won the Democratic nomination against Rep. Seth Moulton, 47, who said that his party needed new leaders.

US.title: North Carolina Rep. Chuck Edwards is formally censured over harassment allegations
US.description: The censure vote drew bipartisan support, and followed an investigation by the House Ethics Committee into allegations of sexual harassment against two young female staff members.

US.title: Congress averts a government shutdown ahead of the midterms
US.description: With just a few weeks to spare, the House approved legislation extending funding through mid-December.

US.title: ICE says it has enough body cameras now, after series of deadly shootings
US.description: Cameras could help alleviate some concerns about ICE transparency and accountability after immigration officers were involved in over two dozen shootings under the Trump administration.

US.title: Beloved writer and environmentalist Wendell Berry has died at age 92
US.description: Wendell Berry has died at age 92 He was a beloved American poet, novelist, essayist, and farmer.

US.title: SCOTUS allows Trump's ballroom project to continue. And, the Army secretary resigns
US.description: The Supreme Court has ruled that President Trump's ballroom project may continue. And, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigns after 18 months on the job.

US.title: They live by a shrine to a saint. Why are their homes being demolished?
US.description: The neighborhood is a pilgrimage site, with a shrine to the Sufi saint known as Bari Imam. In the past year, hundreds of homes of the working poor were razed. Residents fear more will be demolished.

US.title: Why the Supreme Court's ballroom ruling could matter beyond the ballroom
US.description: Georgetown Law professor Stephen Vladeck explains the separation-of-powers questions raised by the Supreme Court's decision on the White House ballroom.

US.title: USPS 'carefully reviewing' whistleblower claim on plan for Trump's mail in voting order
US.description: A whistleblower says the U.S. Postal Service is rushing out an online system for President Trump's push to restrict mail voting that could "derail" the midterm election if courts allow
